title: Insurance Renewal Rage Script
oneLiner: A renewal call room that helps small-business brokers turn premium shock into a clean carrier-shopping and client-explanation packet.
targetUser: Commercial health-insurance brokers, benefits advisors, and very small employers preparing for painful 2026 renewals.
keyUX: Paste current plan and renewal quotes, choose the client anger pattern, compare carrier options, build a contribution tradeoff, rehearse the call, and export a client-ready renewal explanation packet.
sourceSignals: S1 - Reddit r/smallbusiness health insurance quote shock: https://www.reddit.com/r/smallbusiness/comments/1pbs5ri/health_insurance/
S3 - Tradeoffs small-business health insurance cost pressure: https://tradeoffs.org/2026/03/12/it-sucks-spiking-health-insurance-costs-hit-small-businesses/
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web app called "Insurance Renewal Rage Script" for commercial health-insurance brokers, benefits advisors, and very small employers preparing for painful 2026 renewals. The app is based on observed user pull: small employers already compare PEOs and plan downgrades while brokers manually shop carriers, take weekend calls, and explain premium shock. The app should use a renewal negotiation room mechanic around the trigger moment "a 2026 renewal quote lands and the client is angry" and make the first screen communicate "Your client is angry before your options are ready." Use the user's own language: "I need to explain this renewal before they think I failed them." Build the core workflow around current plan, renewal quote, carrier alternatives, employee contribution, objection notes, and renewal deadline, and produce a client-ready renewal explanation packet. Required sections: renewal shock header, current plan vs renewal quote table, carrier-shopping lane, client objection cards, contribution slider, say-this/avoid-this script panel, packet completeness meter, and exportable client memo preview. Emotional pressure to make visible: 자산 방어, budget pain, client churn risk, and embarrassment about worse benefits. Design direction: use the `operator-dense` profile with compact charcoal/fog work surfaces, dense quote comparison rows, crisp deadline chips, 40px controls, one red-orange action accent for unresolved renewal risk, visible empty/error states, and no decorative hero. Avoid generic dashboard framing; make the main interaction feel like a tense renewal call room that turns anger into a defensible packet.
